llm.summary: This skill is an instruction-only A/B test analysis guide with no code, no requested credentials, and no install steps — its declared behavior matches its minimal footprint.

dimensions.detail: Name, description, and SKILL.md all describe A/B test analysis, visualization, and recommendations. There are no unrelated environment variables, binaries, or config paths required that would contradict the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md stays on-topic (import CSV, analyze metric, generate report) and does not instruct reading unrelated files or exfiltrating data. It is an instruction-only skill: the examples call 'openclaw run ab-test-analyzer ...' but there are no implementation files included here, so the instructions are effectively documentation / usage examples rather than runnable code bundled with the skill. This makes the runtime behavior ambiguous until an implementation is provided by the platform.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or download instructions are present; nothing is written to disk by this package itself. Lowest-risk posture for an instruction-only skill.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, credentials, or config paths. That is proportionate for the stated purpose of analyzing uploaded CSV test data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true or any elevated persistence. It is user-invocable and uses the platform's normal invocation model.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This is mostly documentation for how an A/B analysis skill would behave; there is no code bundled and no credentials requested, so direct risk from this package is minimal. Before installing or relying on a runnable implementation, verify where the actual analyzer implementation lives (source/homepage) and inspect its code or install steps. When you first run it, use non-sensitive anonymized test data to confirm it only reads the CSV you provide and does not access other files or external endpoints. If the skill is later updated to include an install script, binaries, or required API keys, re-review those changes carefully (especially any network endpoints, downloads, or new env vars). Also note small metadata inconsistencies (skill.json version/author vs registry version and missing homepage) — these increase uncertainty, so request source or provenance if you need higher assurance.
